reasoning: Mandatory experiment: answer-first hook, 4 slides, a reel with trial set to false. Body and brain topics are our only reliable source of reach, so I picked a new brain-and-senses fact that puts the viewer in the sentence. Your pupils widen when you think hard, a well-replicated effect backed by Kahneman & Beatty 1966, Beatty 1982, Joshi 2016 and Bradley 2008. The hook states the full claim up front, and each slide explains one piece. Music continues the rotation (documentary after lofi), and so does the palette (0 after 4). The caption ends with a share prompt and an opinion-style question, so we can compare question types.
topic: Task-evoked pupil dilation: pupils widen with mental effort, memory load, locus coeruleus, emotion
hook: Your pupils grow when you think hard

slides.title: Effort shows in your eyes
slides.body: Mental math or memorizing a list makes your pupils widen, even when the light around you doesn't change.
slides.image_prompt: Extreme close-up of a glossy eye-like glass sphere with a widening dark center, soft studio light, deep blue background

slides.title: Harder task, bigger pupils
slides.body: In a 1966 study, pupils grew with each extra digit people held in memory, then shrank as they said them back.
slides.image_prompt: Row of glass marbles with dark centers growing larger from left to right, numbers carved as small wooden blocks beside them, clean minimal backdrop
slides.credit: Nutschig at English Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 3.0) via wikimedia

slides.title: A brain alertness hub
slides.body: A tiny brainstem area called the locus coeruleus, which drives alertness, is linked to these pupil changes.
slides.image_prompt: Anatomical brain model on a dark table with a single small glowing point in the brainstem, thin light threads reaching toward a glass eye
slides.credit: YVC Biology Department (CC BY 2.0) via wikimedia

slides.title: Feelings do it too
slides.body: Emotional sounds and images, pleasant or unpleasant, can widen your pupils more than neutral ones.
slides.image_prompt: Glass eye sphere reflecting warm red and cool blue light from two sides, dark center enlarged, moody cinematic lighting

cta: Follow for facts your body hides
caption:
Next time you do mental math, your pupils will quietly get bigger. In a classic 1966 study, they widened with every extra number people tried to hold in memory, then shrank as they recalled them.

The same response shows up with emotional sounds and images. Researchers now use pupil size as a window into how hard your brain is working.

Send this to the friend who says they're 'not even trying'. Do you think you could hide how hard you're thinking?

Beatty J (1982). Task-evoked pupillary responses, processing load, and the structure of processing resources. Psychological Bulletin 91:276-292

Bradley MM, Miccoli L, Escrig MA, Lang PJ (2008). The pupil as a measure of emotional arousal and autonomic activation. Psychophysiology 45:602-607
Partala T, Surakka V (2003). Pupil size variation as an indication of affective processing. Int J Human-Computer Studies 59:185-198
